# Homepage concept visuals

Generated with the built-in image_gen tool. These are temporary monochrome concepts, not actual product captures. The website displays them only in development and Vercel review previews.

Replace the corresponding image import in `web/src/components/home/concept-images.ts` when a final capture is available. Preserve its alt text and responsive sizing; `VisualSlot` also accepts final content through `children`.

## architecture.png

Use case: infographic-diagram. Create a polished raster concept visual for the Kizlo headless WordPress website. Strictly monochrome: near-black #0b0b0b backdrop, charcoal panels, white typography, neutral gray hairline borders. No colored accents, colored syntax, gradient color, people, devices, stock-photo backgrounds, marketing headlines, invented logos, or performance claims. Crisp straight-on interface illustration, flat with subtle depth, generous negative space, very legible limited text. This is an illustrative mockup to guide later real captures, not a literal screenshot. Output ONE standalone image, not a page mockup or collage of unrelated images. Keep all essential content inside the canvas with generous safe margins. Wide horizontal 3:1 composition. A precise three-stage architecture scene: left a compact WordPress content editor card with a W monogram and three content rows; center a smaller code module; right a refined frontend browser card with simple article layout. Fine horizontal connectors with right-pointing arrows between the three. Exact large labels below or within the cards: "WordPress + Kizlo plugin", "Kizlo in your app", "Your frontend". In the center code module show only "{ }" and "Typed APIs". Clear takeaway: content stays in WordPress and Kizlo connects it to the frontend. Keep the scene sparse and secondary, no extra explanatory paragraphs.
